title: Checkpoint: Temples and Churches
objective: After this level you can compare how different faiths shaped their holy buildings.
summary: Holy buildings face somewhere: churches usually east (Old St. Peter's west), mosques toward Mecca, Angkor Wat west. Domes, stone skeletons and sacred mountains were three ways to raise a holy roof.

cards.headline: Chapter 3 finale: every building in this chapter points somewhere.
cards.body: Domes, spires, towers and moats all mattered. But before builders laid a stone, most of them had already decided which way the building would face.

cards.headline: Which way to face
cards.body: Orientation, from Latin oriens, "the rising sun", is a building's position on the east-west axis. Christian churches have usually been built with the apse or high altar at the east end, though Rome's Old St. Peter's faced west. Mosques follow a different rule: the mihrab faces Mecca, whatever direction that is (Level 22). And while the other temples around it face east, Angkor Wat faces west. A holy building has a front door, but it also has a direction.

cards.headline: Temples and Churches: three ways to raise a holy roof

items.label: Domes
points: Hagia Sophia: pendentives turn a square into a circle (Level 21)
St. Peter's: checked with a hanging chain, bound in iron (Level 29)

items.label: Stone skeletons
points: Pointed arches and ribs carry the vault (Level 24)
Flying buttresses take the thrust outside (Level 24)

items.label: Sacred mountains
points: Angkor Wat's towers are Meru's peaks (Level 26)
Kandariya Mahadeva's towers refer to Meru too (Level 28)

cards.headline: Chapter 3 complete
learned: How Gothic builders moved heavy supports outdoors and opened their walls to glass.
How pendentives set Hagia Sophia's dome on a square, and why a steeper dome pushes out less.
Which way holy buildings face, from churches facing east to mosques facing Mecca.
Why temple towers at Angkor Wat and Khajuraho stand for Mount Meru, the sacred mountain.

questions.prompt: Temples and Churches recap: where have Christian churches usually placed the apse or high altar?

options.label: At the west end
options.rationale: Old St. Peter's did, but it was the exception.

options.label: Facing Mecca
options.rationale: That's the rule for a mosque's mihrab.

options.label: In the middle, under the dome
options.rationale: The usual rule puts the apse or altar at the east end.

questions.explanation: Churches have usually been oriented with the apse or high altar at the east end; orientation comes from Latin oriens, the rising sun.

questions.prompt: Temples and Churches recap: why doesn't every mosque's mihrab face the same compass direction?

options.label: It follows the rising sun
options.rationale: That's the church tradition of facing east.

options.label: It faces Mecca, wherever the mosque stands
Each builder chose a direction for the view
options.rationale: The mihrab marks the qibla, the direction of Mecca.

options.label: It points to the nearest minaret
options.rationale: The minaret is for the call to prayer; the mihrab faces Mecca.

questions.explanation: Mosques are oriented so the mihrab faces Mecca, so the compass direction depends on where the mosque is.

questions.prompt: Temples and Churches recap: Angkor Wat models Mount Meru. Unlike the temples around it, which way does it face?

options.label: East
options.rationale: That's the direction the other temples around it face.

questions.explanation: The other temples in the area face east; Angkor Wat faces west.

questions.prompt: Temples and Churches recap: what turns Hagia Sophia's square plan into a circle for its dome?

options.label: Flying buttresses
options.rationale: Those carry Gothic vault thrust outside.

options.label: Pendentives in the four upper corners
A ring of iron chains
options.rationale: Iron rings strengthened St. Peter's dome.

questions.explanation: Pendentives, curved triangles in the upper corners, join into a circle for the dome.

questions.prompt: Temples and Churches recap: at the Hōryū-ji pagoda, what ties the five stories together?

options.label: The central pillar, bolted to every floor
options.rationale: The pillar carries only the spire.

options.label: No column: each story is its own framework
Stone walls running floor to floor
options.rationale: The pagoda is wood, with independent stories.

questions.explanation: No column ties the stories together; each is an independent framework, and the joints can rub and slide.
